Mildly dovish tone. The FOMC cuts the funds rate to 1.50–1.75% and deploys T-bill purchases and repo operations to maintain ample reserves, moves that should support demand and output in line with structural and empirical evidence on monetary transmission (e.g., McCallum and Nelson, 1999; Sims and Zha). Yet the statement flags weak business fixed investment and soft exports—investment is a key driver of business-cycle fluctuations and real GDP in standard models, so this is a meaningful headwind. With overall and core inflation below 2% and market-based inflation compensation low, the risk that inflation expectations drift down—central in inflation-targeting frameworks (Svensson) and expectations dynamics (Cagan)—tempers optimism. Strong household spending and a low unemployment rate are supportive, but ongoing uncertainties and two dissenting votes keep the balance of risks cautious. Net effect: slightly positive, but guarded.
